entry.evidence: the TSD power spectra over both the Gulf of Mexico and the eastern U.S. coast have more significant peaks on shorter timescales (10–30 days)

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text) with published PDF for figures

steps.action: Take from prior studies the expectation that the 30–60-day MJO is the main subseasonal control on Gulf of Mexico TC activity and landfall.
steps.quote: has been demonstrated to play an important role in modulating the TC activity in the Gulf of Mexico

steps.action: Compute power spectra of 3-day running mean tropical storm days over the Gulf of Mexico and the eastern U.S. coast.
steps.quote: the TSD power spectra over both the Gulf of Mexico and the eastern U.S. coast have more significant peaks on shorter timescales (10–30 days)

steps.action: Compare the observed spectral peaks with the MJO timescale and find that the dominant peaks lie at 10–30 days, shorter than the MJO.
steps.quote: more significant peaks on shorter timescales (10–30 days) [...]

steps.action: Hypothesize that previously unknown processes regulate the observed subseasonal TC variability.
steps.quote: hypothesize that some previously unknown processes and mechanisms regulate the observed subseasonal variability of TCs

steps.action: Set the aim: identify the major processes controlling subseasonal TC activity near U.S. coasts and test their predictability in a new dynamical model.
steps.quote: [...] this research is to identify the major processes controlling the subseasonal TC activity near the U.S. coasts

steps.action: Choose lower-tropospheric (850 hPa) circulation as the target field, on the grounds that it approximates steering flow and that low-level vorticity dominates subseasonal genesis in the western North Atlantic.
steps.quote: Motivated by this, we focus on understanding the major atmospheric circulation modes in the lower troposphere

steps.action: Run an EOF analysis of observed (ERA-5) 3-day running mean H850 anomalies for June–October over 100°W–70°W, 10°N–40°N, yielding three leading modes.
steps.quote: This analysis yields three distinctive modes that explain about 49.4%, 17.6%, and 13.9% of the total H850 variance.

steps.action: Check the modes over a 4.4-times larger domain and test whether they arise from TC-related H850 anomalies within 500 km of storm centres; both checks are reported in Methods.
steps.quote: Note that these three leading modes are still present over a much larger domain (see Methods).

steps.action: Establish that the PCs of all three modes have significant 10–30-day spectral peaks against red noise and are distinct from the 30–60-day MJO and BSISO.
steps.quote: reveals significant peaks on the subseasonal timescale (10–30 day) relative to a red noise process

steps.action: Recompute the EOFs from band-pass filtered (10–35 day) H850 anomalies and obtain similar patterns.
steps.quote: confirming the predominance and robustness of the subseasonal components

steps.action: Build simple box-average H850 indices as surrogates for the three modes and check their correlation with the PCs (r = 0.99, 0.97, 0.95).
steps.quote: Some simple indices can be constructed as a surrogate for these three modes and they are highly correlated with the PCs

steps.action: Propose that PO and GAD are linked to midlatitude transient eddies and Rossby wave breaking, and that SHR is linked to variation of the NASH centre.
steps.quote: their formation and evolution are likely linked to the transient eddies that develop in the midlatitude baroclinic zones

steps.action: Show that the modes also appear on synoptic timescales, with a weaker modulation of coastal TCs.
steps.quote: These three modes are also robust on synoptic timescales

steps.action: Composite TC genesis, tracks, TSDs, landfall rates (Table 1) and intensity over strong positive, neutral and negative phases of each mode, 1979–2018.
steps.quote: the U.S. East Coast experiences 19 times more LTCs during the strong positive phases of PO

steps.action: Test the landfall-rate and TC-precipitation differences against a bootstrap null distribution.
steps.quote: we use the bootstrap method to shuffle the data

steps.action: Composite precipitation and 500 hPa wind differences between the strong phases of each mode, with t-test significance.
steps.quote: The rainfall anomalies differ dramatically among these three modes

steps.action: Estimate the share of the rainfall anomalies caused by TCs (grid points within 500 km of storm centres) and their contribution to heavy rainfall.
steps.quote: TC-induced rainfall anomalies can explain about 20–50% of the total rainfall anomalies

steps.action: Explain the modulation through changes in steering flow and in low-level relative vorticity, with vertical motion a secondary factor and shear less important.
steps.quote: First, they largely alter the steering flows as well as TC landfall probability.

steps.action: Qualify the relation by season: GAD modulation is stronger in summer, PO and SHR modulation stronger in autumn.
steps.quote: The links between TC activity and these modes display salient seasonal dependence.

steps.action: Ask how well a dynamical model simulates the modes and how far ahead they can be predicted.
steps.quote: Whether and to what extent can these modes be predicted?

steps.action: Analyse a 50-year GFDL SPEAR control simulation for the three modes.
steps.quote: From a 50-yr control simulation

steps.action: Check that the model reproduces the observed spatial patterns, power spectra and TC modulation of the modes.
steps.quote: the model well captures these three modes, with similar spatial patterns, power spectra (Supplementary Fig. 8), and also TC [...]

steps.action: Use 20-year (2000–2019) SPEAR hindcasts (720 cases, 10 members) from the authors' earlier work, projected onto the observed EOFs.
steps.quote: Based on 20-yr (2000–2019) hindcast results using the SPEAR model41

steps.action: Score the hindcast PCs with ACC and with MSSS against a climatological reference, giving skilful lead times of 13, 9 and 22 days.
steps.quote: these three modes (PO, GAD, SHR) can be skillfully predicted with a lead time of 13, 9, and 22 days, respectively

steps.action: Use lead-lag relations with H500 and precipitation to reject remote (tropical) forcing, concluding that the modes are locally excited and independent of MJO, BSISO, NAO and PNA.
steps.quote: This implies that all these modes are locally excited and maintained, largely independent from other modes

steps.action: Keep the claim that three subseasonal modes strongly modulate TC activity near the U.S. coast.
steps.quote: We have identified three major subseasnonal modes (Fig. 6) that show strong modulation on the TC activities near the U.S. coast.

end.claim: Three localized 10–30-day lower-tropospheric circulation modes (PO, GAD, SHR) strongly modulate TC genesis, track, intensity, landfall and rainfall near the U.S. coast in June–October 1979–2018, with up to 19 times more East Coast landfalls in strong positive versus negative PO phases.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the phase composites of TC landfall rates (Table 1) and tracks, the EOF modes would be circulation patterns with no demonstrated link to landfalling TCs.

gates.evidence: The hypothesis of unknown 10–30-day processes (§1 ¶5) directed the choice of analysis, but all data were pre-existing reanalysis, best-track and hindcast archives. The claim faced red-noise spectral tests and bootstrap and t-test nulls it could have failed (§2.1 ¶3, §4.6 ¶1), but no crucial test against stated rivals. Domain, filters, thresholds (|PC|>1) and skill criteria are not stated as fixed in advance.

imports.item: Bootstrap resampling significance test and t-test
Power spectra tested against a red-noise null with confidence limits

novelty_claims.quote: This work reveals three localized atmospheric circulation modes with significant 10–30 days subseasonal variations
hypothesize that some previously unknown processes and mechanisms regulate the observed subseasonal variability of TCs
So far, there is little evidence in the literature of skillful subseasonal LTC prediction near the U.S. coast.

limits: No review file or supplement was supplied, so the many supplementary checks (Supp. Figs 1–12, Supp. Table 1) are coded from main-text descriptions only. Methods states "we conduct a lot of tests" but reports only one domain test; the other tests and any failures are not shown. The SPEAR hindcasts were produced in the authors' earlier work (ref. 41); only their scoring is done here. Sub-claim statuses: predictability of 13, 9 and 22 days for the modes is close to forecast_skill (scored against a climatological reference with MSSS), but the hindcasts are retrospective and skill is reported for the modes, not for TC landfalls. The mechanisms (steering flow, vorticity, RWB, NASH link) are best_explanation at most and partly stated as "likely". The local-forcing conclusion is inferred from lead-lag patterns, not from a set experiment. The choices of number of modes, the |PC|>1 threshold and the 10–35-day filter are not justified against alternatives, and no multiple-testing correction is reported. Inference: the acknowledgements thank Drs. Murakami, Johnson and Wang for review comments, which suggests an internal (GFDL) review whose effects cannot be coded.

disagreements.target: Prior studies (refs 27–31) presenting the MJO as the crucial source of subseasonal TC predictability in the Gulf
disagreements.support: TSD spectra peak at 10–30 days rather than MJO timescales, and the three modes are distinct from and independent of the MJO and BSISO (Supp. Table 1).
disagreements.quote: Although these previous studies would suggest the MJO as a crucial source of subseasonal TSD predictability

disagreements.target: Maloney & Hartmann (2000): MJO mode originating from the eastern Pacific modulating Gulf hurricanes
disagreements.support: The SHR modulation pattern resembles the MJO pattern but operates on a shorter timescale.
disagreements.quote: exhibits a similar pattern with an MJO mode originating from the eastern Pacific29, but they differ in timescales

disagreements.target: Interannual-to-decadal controls on U.S. LTCs (ENSO, AMO, NAO, PMM, SST; refs 2, 16–24)
disagreements.support: The subseasonal modes are locally excited and offer mechanisms that differ from those of lower-frequency controls.
disagreements.quote: differing substantially from that for the interannual to decadal variations

disagreements.target: Community position that dynamical models give useful TC prediction only within about 1 week (refs 11–15)
disagreements.support: SPEAR hindcasts predict the controlling modes skilfully for 9–22 days, which the authors read as an opportunity for subseasonal LTC prediction; TC skill itself is not tested.
disagreements.quote: The majority of current dynamical models only show useful TC prediction in terms of genesis and tropical storm days (TSDs)
